title: The Case of Sacco and Vanzetti
summary: Josh and Chuck cover the case of Nicola Sacco and Bartolomeo Vanzetti, Italian immigrant anarchists convicted of the April 1920 payroll robbery and murders in Braintree, Massachusetts. They walk through the crime, the arrests on a train in Brockton, the weak circumstantial evidence (eyewitnesses, guns, a hat, ballistics), the defense and prosecution maneuvering, Judge Thayer's rulings, the Celestino Madeiros confession, the Lowell Commission, the 1927 executions, and later revelations about Fred Moore, Carlo Tresca, and the bullet evidence. The episode closes with a listener mail segment about Black Loyalists and Rhode Island's slave history.

segments.title: Intro and historical context
segments.summary: Hosts introduce the Sacco and Vanzetti case, the anarchist movement, the Galleani connection, and the 1920s Red Scare and anarchist violence in the US and abroad.

segments.title: Braintree payroll robbery
segments.summary: Shelley Neil, an American Express agent, picks up payroll for shoe companies in Braintree. Paymaster Frederick Parmenter and guard Alessandro Berardelli are shot on Pearl Street, and about fifteen thousand dollars is taken by men in a blue car. Witnesses describe the car and a gunman in a felt cap.

segments.title: Car found and Coccioli deportation
segments.summary: The getaway car is found in the woods in Bridgewater with plates removed. Ferruccio Coacci, an anarchist facing deportation, fails to appear and gives a false sick-wife excuse, drawing suspicion.

segments.title: Police chief Stewart and Boda investigation
segments.summary: Police Chief Michael Stewart examines Mike Boda's garage and finds large tire tracks. Boda flees when a visit to the garage turns tense, and Sacco and Vanzetti are later seen leaving on foot toward a rail line.

segments.title: Arrest on the train in Brockton
segments.summary: Sacco and Vanzetti are taken off a train in Brockton and found carrying guns, a Colt automatic and a Harrington and Richardson revolver, along with anarchist pamphlets. Their stories are inconsistent, and they are taken to Braintree for questioning by Chief Stewart and prosecutor Katzmann.

segments.title: Defense campaign and trial
segments.summary: Anarchists form the Sacco-Vanzetti Defense Committee and hire Fred Moore. Moore builds an international publicity campaign. Judge Webster Thayer presides over the trial, where the case rests on circumstantial evidence, eyewitnesses, and ballistics testimony from amateur experts.

segments.title: Hat evidence, gun testimony, and verdict
segments.summary: Discussion of the gray cap evidence and how the hat was linked to Sacco, the questionable chain of custody, the gun testimony about Vanzetti, and the jury verdict of guilty after about five and a half hours of deliberation. International protests follow.

segments.title: Appeals and Madeiros confession
segments.summary: Moore and later William Thompson file repeated appeals and motions, all denied, including a claim of judicial bias. Celestino Madeiros confesses to the crime while in prison and says Sacco and Vanzetti were not there, but the confession is rejected. The Lowell Commission reports the men guilty.

segments.title: Execution and aftermath
segments.summary: Sacco and Vanzetti are executed in the electric chair at Charlestown State Prison in 1927 under heavy security. Riots and protests occur in Germany, Geneva, and Paris. Later revelations include Carlo Tresca's view, a 1961 ballistics test, and Upton Sinclair's accounts of Fred Moore's statements.

segments.title: Wrap-up
segments.summary: Hosts summarize the case and suggest further reading, including Douglas Linder's work.

segments.title: Listener mail on Black Loyalists and Rhode Island slavery
segments.summary: A listener writes about Nova Scotia and Black Loyalists, and corrects the hosts that Rhode Island was the first state to abolish slavery but had a large slave trade in Newport.
